blocks.text: Easter Island: Anakena and Major Archaeological Sites

provenance.rationale: The itinerary title summarizes the authorized Word Day 9 full-day Anakena archaeological excursion.

blocks.text:
Breakfast at the hotel. Anakena — Full-Day Excursion During this excursion, we will visit several archaeological sites, allowing us to learn about the development of Rapa Nui culture, including its origins, flourishing period, and most difficult crises. We will travel along the coast and visit Ahu Akahanga, followed by a visit to Rano Raraku Volcano and its slopes, where most of the Moai statues were carved and where the largest number of these statues can still be found today.

Box lunch in the countryside. We will then visit Ahu Tongariki, the island's largest ceremonial platform, featuring 15 restored statues. The excursion continues to the Poike Peninsula, located on the northern coast, with a stop at Ahu Te Pito Kura. This site is home to the largest Moai statue ever erected outside the quarry and is also considered an important energy center of the island.

We then travel to Anakena Beach, with its warm turquoise waters, white sand, palm trees, and the Ahu Nau Nau ceremonial platform, creating one of the island's most beautiful and attractive landscapes. Time to walk along the beach and enjoy a swim. Return to the village of Hanga Roa via a road crossing the center of the island. Duration: Full day
